paragraphs: This paper studies clustering when the objects are lines rather than individual points. The aim is to choose k centers that minimize the total squared distance from each line to its nearest center. This setting matters for applications involving structured geometric information, where methods developed for collections of points do not transfer straightforwardly.

The authors adapt local search, which improves a solution by replacing a center. Two obstacles make this difficult: point-to-line distances lack the triangle inequality needed by familiar analyses, and infinitely extending lines make useful replacement locations hard to identify. Their proportional capture relation connects current and optimal centers through line-assignment proportions. A second construction, CrossLine, discretizes space around pairs of lines while retaining high-quality replacement candidates.

Together, these components yield what the authors identify as the first single-swap local search algorithm for this problem. In low-dimensional Euclidean space, it runs in polynomial time and provides a 500-plus-epsilon approximation guarantee. That is a theoretical bound on solution quality relative to the optimum, rather than a reported typical error or empirical accuracy.
neurips-2025-a-single-swap-local-search-.tldr: A new geometric analysis enables polynomial-time single-swap local search with a 500-plus-epsilon approximation guarantee for clustering lines in low dimensions.

paragraphs: Protein generators often learn from structures predicted by AlphaFold2 because experimentally determined structures are relatively scarce. This creates a quality problem: errors in the predicted training structures can constrain what the generator learns. The abstract highlights long, complex proteins as particularly challenging because AlphaFold2 predictions become less accurate as protein length and complexity increase.

Ambient Protein Diffusion treats low-confidence predicted structures as corrupted observations. Instead of discarding them, it changes the diffusion training objective according to each structure's corruption level. The model can therefore learn from structures of varying quality while accounting for their differing reliability. The central contribution is a way to use imperfect training material without treating every predicted structure as equally trustworthy.

For proteins containing 700 residues, the authors report diversity rising from 45% to 85% relative to the previous state of the art, alongside designability increasing from 70% to 88%. These empirical results support the approach for the reported long-protein setting. They connect the treatment of noisy training structures to improvements in both the variety and designability of generated structures.
neurips-2025-ambient-proteins-training-d.tldr: Ambient Protein Diffusion adjusts training to account for unreliable predicted structures, improving reported diversity and designability for long proteins.

paragraphs: APIGen-MT addresses the shortage of training conversations that capture realistic interactions between people and AI agents over multiple turns. Such data must represent how a task develops through an exchange, including the actions an agent should take. Collecting these examples manually is expensive, motivating a synthetic generation process with explicit checks on its contents.

The framework separates planning an interaction from writing out the conversation. First, it constructs detailed task blueprints containing ground-truth actions. A committee of language-model reviewers and repeated feedback help refine these plans. Second, simulated human-agent interactions expand the blueprints into complete trajectories. This ordering gives the generated dialogue an action-level reference against which its task progression can be checked.

The authors use the data to train the xLAM-2-fc-r family, spanning 1B to 70B parameters. On τ-bench and BFCL, they report results above GPT-4o and Claude 3.5, with smaller models surpassing larger counterparts particularly in multi-turn settings and showing stronger consistency across trials. These findings support the value of verified synthetic interaction data in the evaluated agent tasks. The data and models are released openly.
neurips-2025-apigen-mt-agentic-pipeline-.tldr: APIGen-MT builds reviewed task blueprints and simulated conversations to train agents with strong multi-turn benchmark performance.

paragraphs: STARK evaluates how language models reason about signals that vary across space and time, a capability relevant to cyber-physical systems. Its hierarchy distinguishes estimating states, reasoning about relationships between states, and combining those relationships with world knowledge. This separates problems such as tracking an event from more contextual tasks such as inferring intent or navigating using landmarks.

The benchmark contains 26 tasks and 14,552 challenges across diverse sensor modalities. Models answer either directly or through a Python Code Interpreter. The authors evaluate eight language models and three reasoning models. Ordinary language models have limited success on geometric tasks such as triangulation, especially as complexity grows, while reasoning models often match or exceed traditional methods based on first principles.

The pattern changes when tasks require world knowledge: the gap narrows, and some language models outperform reasoning models. Nevertheless, o3 leads across all evaluated tasks; the authors attribute this primarily to reasoning-model size. The benchmark therefore reveals differences across types of reasoning, rather than reducing spatiotemporal competence to a single undifferentiated capability.
neurips-2025-benchmarking-spatiotemporal.tldr: STARK tests spatial and temporal reasoning across 26 tasks, finding strong reasoning-model results but smaller advantages on tasks requiring world knowledge.

paragraphs: CAS-Spec aims to accelerate language-model generation through lossless speculative decoding. Existing approaches that construct drafts on the fly are convenient to integrate, but often deliver smaller speed gains than methods requiring specialized training. Using several draft models could improve flexibility, yet training a separate hierarchy of models introduces a substantial practical cost.

The proposed method creates draft models through dynamically switchable inference strategies, including layer sparsity and activation quantization. It then coordinates these models with Dynamic Tree Cascade. This algorithm adapts both which draft levels to use and how long their drafts should be, using acceptance-rate heuristics and predicted latency. The coordination matters because conventional cascade arrangements are inefficient for the self-speculative setting considered here.

Across the evaluated models and datasets, CAS-Spec reports average speedups ranging from 1.1 to 2.3 times ordinary autoregressive decoding. Dynamic Tree Cascade improves average speedup by 47% over a cascade baseline and 48% over a tree baseline. These results support adaptive coordination as a useful part of acceleration, alongside the cheaper draft computations themselves, within the reported lossless decoding framework.
neurips-2025-cas-spec-cascade-adaptive-s.tldr: CAS-Spec combines dynamically constructed draft models with adaptive tree routing to accelerate lossless language-model decoding without specialized draft-model training.

paragraphs: Some reinforcement-learning tasks require an agent to choose both a discrete action and continuous parameters associated with that action. In safety-critical applications, the agent must also respect cost constraints. The paper addresses this combination, which is difficult for existing hybrid-action methods focused primarily on maximizing reward rather than jointly handling reward and constraints.

The authors formalize the problem as a Constrained Parameterized-action Markov Decision Process. This formulation puts parameterized action choices and safety constraints into the same decision-making objective. They then introduce Constrained Hybrid-action Policy Optimization, or CHPO, to solve problems in this framework. Its purpose is to optimize how the agent acts while accounting for the constraints that determine acceptable behavior.

The paper's theoretical analysis establishes convergence to an optimal solution while satisfying safety constraints in the analyzed formulation. Experiments across multiple tasks report competitive performance. These are complementary contributions: the analysis addresses the relationship between optimization and constraint satisfaction, while the experiments assess how the algorithm performs on concrete tasks. The stated guarantee concerns the mathematical setting studied in the paper.
neurips-2025-chpo-constrained-hybrid-act.tldr: CHPO combines discrete-continuous action selection with cost constraints, with theoretical convergence results and competitive experimental performance.

paragraphs: This paper investigates whether patterns across a network's neural activity reflect regularities in its training data. The authors call this the Reflection Hypothesis and present evidence in recurrent neural networks and large language models. Their interpretability strategy is to divide high-dimensional activity into recurring, meaningful units, drawing on the cognitive idea of chunking.

Three methods accommodate different kinds of available information. Discrete sequence chunking builds a dictionary of entities in a lower-dimensional neural space. Population averaging uses known labels to extract recurring entities. Unsupervised chunk discovery operates without labels. Together, these methods provide ways to look for concept-related activity patterns across models and settings with different annotation and dimensionality constraints.

The authors report correspondence between extracted entities and concrete or abstract concepts, with examples ranging from compositionality in recurrent networks to recurring states across language-model architectures. They also intervene by artificially inducing extracted entities, which changes generation of the associated concepts. That intervention connects the discovered activity patterns to model behavior, extending the evidence beyond simply observing that a pattern and a concept appear together.
neurips-2025-concept-guided-interpretabi.tldr: Neural chunking extracts recurring concept-related activity patterns, and inducing those patterns changes the concepts networks generate.

paragraphs: Adversarial examples developed against one model often fail against another. This paper attributes that difficulty to differences in decision boundaries and shifts in internal feature representations. For untargeted attacks, it proposes optimizing perturbations to remain effective across a neighborhood of plausible target models, rather than relying on the exact behavior of a single model.

CORTA represents this uncertainty through two complementary channels. Weight perturbations capture possible changes in decision boundaries, while stochastic blending of clean and adversarial activations represents feature drift. Its practical implementation combines a sensitivity regularizer based on how output logits respond to weights with Monte Carlo sampling of blended features. Theoretical analysis supplies a certified lower bound connecting these approximations to the robust objective.

Experiments on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet report stronger transfer attacks across convolutional and Vision Transformer targets than prior methods, including ensemble approaches. The abstract highlights a 19.1 percentage-point improvement over the best previous method using one surrogate model. The result supports modeling several kinds of target uncertainty within a single-surrogate attack, with the claim specifically concerning untargeted transfer attacks.
neurips-2025-consensus-robust-transfer-a.tldr: CORTA models uncertainty in both weights and internal representations to improve the transferability of untargeted adversarial attacks.

paragraphs: Training-free federated learning can combine summaries of client data to construct a global classifier without training it. Class means provide a compact summary, while covariance matrices describe additional variation within classes but require more communication. This paper asks whether the server can benefit from that richer information when clients send only their class means.

The authors propose an unbiased estimator of class covariance matrices based on the communicated means. The server uses these estimates to initialize the global classifier, gaining access to covariance information without receiving covariance matrices directly. They also find that restricting initialization to within-class covariances produces a better classifier. The method makes the distribution of client means useful beyond simply supplying average class representations.

The reported performance improvement over methods that share only means is 4–26%, at the same communication cost. Results are competitive with or better than approaches transmitting second-order statistics, with much less communication, and also exceed the compared federated prompt-tuning methods. The initialization remains useful when followed by federated fine-tuning or linear probing, showing benefits beyond the training-free configuration.
neurips-2025-covariances-for-free-exploi.tldr: Estimating class covariances from client class means improves federated classifier initialization without increasing the communication required by mean-only methods.

paragraphs: Understanding activity in an operating room requires following interactions among people and equipment despite frequent visual obstruction. EgoExOR combines first-person recordings with third-person views to provide complementary perspectives on those interactions. The dataset is designed to support surgical activity understanding and human-centered perception through a richer combination of views and sensor signals.

Its recordings cover 94 minutes of two emulated spine procedures: ultrasound-guided needle insertion and minimally invasive spine surgery. Wearable glasses supply RGB video, gaze, hand tracking, and audio, while external cameras provide RGB and depth; ultrasound imagery is also included. Scene graph annotations describe entities and their relationships, covering 36 entities, 22 relation types, and 568,235 annotated triplets.

The paper evaluates two adapted models for surgical scene graph generation and introduces a baseline that explicitly uses the dataset's multiple modalities and perspectives. Its main contribution is therefore both a resource and an evaluation setting for modeling clinical interactions. The recordings come from two emulated procedures, which defines the concrete procedural setting represented by the dataset rather than a broad collection of operating-room cases.
neurips-2025-egoexor-an-ego-exo-centric-.tldr: EgoExOR combines wearable and external sensor views with detailed interaction annotations for studying activity in two emulated surgical procedures.

paragraphs: HYPERION addresses federated graph learning when some training labels are noisy. Graph connections make this difficult because errors can propagate along edges, and examples belonging to the same class can still occupy different structural positions. The paper argues that previous robust federated approaches do not adequately address both of these graph-specific problems.

At each client, the method uses a hyperspherical representation to capture graph structure at a fine level of detail. Alignment within this space addresses error propagation and structural differences within classes. At the server, a geometric-aware purification module targets noise that remains undetected because individual clients have only localized perspectives. Both components operate in a shared hyperspherical space, connecting local processing with server-level correction.

The authors report robustness across multiple datasets. One highlighted result is a 29.7% increase in macro F1 on Cora with 50% pair noise. This example supports the combined client-and-server approach under the tested noisy-label setting. The broader contribution is to make structural information central to robustness at both levels, rather than handling label corruption independently of how examples are connected.
neurips-2025-hyperion-fine-grained-hyper.tldr: HYPERION combines client-side hypersphere alignment with server-side purification to improve federated graph learning under noisy labels.

paragraphs: LoRA adapts language models through parameter-efficient modifications, but supporting adaptation and inference together presents a runtime challenge. Loquetier addresses this by unifying LoRA fine-tuning and serving within one framework. The aim is to support multiple adapters on a shared base model while making their different computational workloads work efficiently together.

The framework has two main components. A Virtualized Module isolates the adapter-specific modifications, allowing multiple adapters to coexist around the common model. An optimized computation flow and kernel design merge fine-tuning and inference paths during forward propagation. This makes batching more efficient and reduces kernel invocation overhead, directly targeting the runtime cost of handling these workloads together.

Across three task settings, the authors report gains in performance and flexibility over existing baselines. For inference-only workloads, throughput reaches up to three times that of the compared state-of-the-art co-serving system. For combined fine-tuning and inference, service-level objective attainment is reported as 46.4 times higher than PEFT. These measurements describe different operational benefits: processing capacity in one setting and meeting service objectives in another.
neurips-2025-loquetier-a-virtualized-mul.tldr: Loquetier shares a base model across LoRA adapters and merges computation paths to improve unified fine-tuning and inference.

paragraphs: MOGO explores whether video action detection can be handled efficiently by an architecture built entirely from Mamba. Mamba's near-linear sequence-modeling complexity motivates its use for video, where information spans multiple frames. The framework uses neither Transformer components nor RCNN-like proposal detection, and its decoder can perform the task with just one Mamba layer.

Its encoder combines information across frames, while the decoder contains two newly designed Mamba-based structures for detecting actions. The authors use theoretical analysis and ablations to support the contribution of each structure and their combined operation. A separate video-token construction mechanism includes a token importance block, keeping the retained information relevant to the targets the model must predict.

On JHMDB and UCF101-24, MOGO reports comparable detection precision to state-of-the-art methods while improving computational cost, parameter count, and inference latency. It also uses substantially less GPU memory than some token reconstruction methods. The findings support an efficiency-focused alternative for the evaluated detection tasks: architectural simplification and selective token information preserve competitive precision while reducing several kinds of resource use.
neurips-2025-mamba-only-glances-once-mog.tldr: MOGO uses an entirely Mamba-based architecture to achieve competitive video action detection precision with lower compute, parameter count, and latency.

paragraphs: A multi-view Gaussian process latent variable model learns a unified representation from data with multiple views. Its usefulness depends partly on the kernel, which determines the relationships the model can express. This paper targets two obstacles together: kernels that are insufficiently expressive and the computational expense of learning a shared latent representation.

The authors introduce a duality between a kernel function and its spectral density. Modeling that density with a bivariate Gaussian mixture yields their Next-Gen Spectral Mixture kernel. To make this expressive construction more computationally manageable, they approximate it with random Fourier features. A tailored reparameterization method then enables scalable variational inference for both the model and the latent representations it learns.

Evaluations on diverse multi-view datasets report consistently better latent-representation learning than the compared state-of-the-art models. The approach matters because expressiveness and efficiency are addressed as connected design problems: the richer kernel supplies modeling flexibility, while its approximation supports practical inference. The reported findings indicate that this combination produces meaningful shared representations in the datasets studied.
neurips-2025-multi-view-oriented-gplvm-e.tldr: A more expressive spectral-mixture kernel and scalable approximation improve shared representation learning from multi-view data.

paragraphs: Bandit convex optimization studies repeated decisions where a learner chooses an action from a continuous domain and observes only the loss at that point, without its gradient. This paper considers changing environments. It measures change through switches in the comparison sequence, variation in loss functions, and the distance traveled by the comparison sequence.

For strongly convex losses, the authors introduce TEWA-SE, a polynomial-time algorithm that adapts sleeping experts to bandit feedback. They prove matching upper and lower regret bounds when the number of switches or total loss variation is known, establishing minimax optimality for those measures. Adding a Bandit-over-Bandit framework extends the analysis to cases where the amount of non-stationarity is unknown.

For general convex losses, a second algorithm, cExO, uses exponential weighting over a discretized action space. It achieves minimax-optimal regret for known switches and loss variation, and improves existing path-length bounds. However, it is not polynomial-time computable. The results therefore distinguish statistical guarantees from computational efficiency, with the stronger efficiency result tied to the strongly convex setting.
neurips-2025-non-stationary-bandit-conve.tldr: Two algorithms establish strong regret guarantees for changing bandit convex optimization problems, with computational efficiency depending on the loss setting.

paragraphs: Graph anomaly detectors can learn to rely on homophily, the tendency for connected examples to resemble one another. That reliance becomes fragile when a new graph has less homophily than the training graph. The paper addresses structural distribution shifts of this kind, aiming to find predictive patterns that remain useful as connection patterns change.

HEM first separates the learning of an example's own features from the learning of its neighborhood structure. This disentangling supports efforts to make structural representations more stable. A homophily-aware environment mixup then changes edge weights through adversarial learning, generating environments with different structural distributions. The classifier and environment generator train iteratively, combining more diverse training structures with a search for invariant predictive information.

Experiments on real-world datasets report state-of-the-art performance under structural distribution shifts. The central idea is to challenge the detector with changing graph relationships during training, reducing its reliance on structural regularities that may disappear later. Separating feature and neighborhood representations gives the method a way to address the unstable structural component while learning from both sources of information.
neurips-2025-out-of-distribution-general.tldr: HEM separates feature and neighborhood learning and generates varied graph environments to improve anomaly detection under structural shifts.

paragraphs: World models can help multi-agent reinforcement learning use experience more efficiently, but predicting environments with many agents is difficult. Joint action spaces grow exponentially, and interactions introduce uncertain dynamics. This paper changes the modeling problem by focusing on the state space at each timestep and incorporating agents' actions sequentially rather than modeling the full joint transition together.

Sequential agent modeling progressively resolves uncertainty while retaining dependencies among agents. The authors connect this gradual revelation of actions to the reverse process in diffusion models. They use that connection to construct DIMA, a diffusion-inspired multi-agent world model. The approach makes the order in which action information enters the model part of how it represents agents' combined influence on the state.

Across multiple control benchmarks, including MAMuJoCo and Bi-DexHands, DIMA reports state-of-the-art results and improvements over earlier world models in final return and sample efficiency. These findings support the proposed modeling strategy in the evaluated settings. Its contribution is both a reformulation of the multi-agent prediction problem and a diffusion-based implementation that uses that reformulation to support policy learning.
neurips-2025-revisiting-multi-agent-worl.tldr: DIMA uses diffusion-inspired sequential agent modeling to improve world-model accuracy and multi-agent learning efficiency on evaluated control benchmarks.

paragraphs: ShapeCraft addresses a practical problem in text-to-3D generation: a generated object may look useful but remain difficult to edit because its mesh lacks meaningful structure. The paper represents assets as shape programs, aiming to produce objects that support continued modeling, painting, and interaction within artistic workflows rather than ending at an unstructured geometric output.

Its Graph-based Procedural Shape representation organizes a complex language request into a graph of modeling subtasks. Multiple language-model agents parse the request hierarchically to initialize this graph, then iteratively refine the procedural geometry and painting. The structured representation helps the agents interpret spatial relationships and semantic shape details, connecting what the user describes to the operations that build the asset.

Qualitative and quantitative experiments report better geometric accuracy and semantic richness than existing language-model-based agents. The authors also demonstrate animation and user-customized editing. Those examples illustrate why the representation matters beyond initial generation: the asset retains a structure that can support further interaction. The findings establish reported advantages within the evaluated comparisons and demonstrate potential for broader interactive applications.
neurips-2025-shapecraft-llm-agents-for-s.tldr: ShapeCraft turns text into procedural shape graphs that language-model agents refine into structured, textured, and editable 3D assets.

paragraphs: SMMILE tests whether multimodal language models can learn medical tasks from examples supplied in their immediate context. This differs from simply answering a medical image question: the demonstrations are meant to help the model adapt to the particular task. Eleven medical experts curated problems containing both a multimodal query and multimodal task examples.

The benchmark includes 111 problems built from 517 question-image-answer triplets, spanning six medical specialties and 13 imaging modalities. An augmented version, SMMILE++, contains 1,038 permuted problems. Across 15 models, the authors find mostly moderate to poor ability to learn from these demonstrations. In open-ended evaluations, examples improve performance over zero-shot prompting by an average of 8% on SMMILE and 9.4% on SMMILE++.

The choice and ordering of examples also matter substantially. A single irrelevant or noisy example can reduce performance by up to 9.5%, while placing the most relevant example last can improve it by up to 71%. These findings reveal sensitivity to demonstration quality and recency, showing that the benefit of medical examples depends strongly on how they are presented.
neurips-2025-smmile-an-expert-driven-ben.tldr: SMMILE finds that medical learning from multimodal examples is often weak and strongly affected by irrelevant examples and their ordering.

paragraphs: This paper applies spiking neural networks to increasing the resolution of remote sensing images. Such networks offer energy-efficiency potential, but limited representational capacity can hinder their usefulness. The authors observe that spike intensity varies sharply across image textures, motivating an attention mechanism that shapes spiking activity to better represent information needed for reconstruction.

Their spiking attention block adjusts membrane potentials using inferred attention weights, thereby regulating spikes. It connects temporal and channel modulation so that their relationships can be learned jointly. It also draws on globally recurring patterns in large remote sensing images to derive spatial attention weights. These self-similar patterns provide reconstruction guidance tied to the imagery's structure.

The resulting model, SpikeSR, reports state-of-the-art performance across remote sensing benchmarks including AID, DOTA, and DIOR while maintaining high computational efficiency. The contribution links attention directly to the internal operation of spiking neurons, using it to improve their feature representation. The reported results support this combination as an effective approach to remote sensing super-resolution in the evaluated datasets.
neurips-2025-spiking-meets-attention-eff.tldr: SpikeSR uses attention to regulate spiking neurons and exploit repeated image patterns for efficient remote sensing super-resolution.

paragraphs: Backdoor attacks poison training data so that a trigger can later influence a model's predictions. For graph classification, an attacker must affect the representation of an entire graph while keeping the poisoned examples inconspicuous. This paper examines why existing graph-level attacks can stand out to anomaly detectors despite being designed to remain stealthy.

The authors identify two sources of detectable mismatch. Rare trigger subgraphs introduce unusual structure, while changing labels creates a mismatch between a graph's content and its assigned class. DPSBA addresses these through a clean-label framework that learns triggers intended to remain within the data distribution. Adversarial training uses anomaly-aware discriminators to guide the learning process and suppress structural and semantic anomalies.

Experiments on real-world datasets report high attack success alongside improved stealth, producing a better effectiveness-detectability balance than the compared state-of-the-art methods. The findings show that suppressing the cues used by anomaly detection can coexist with effective graph-level backdoors in the tested settings. The stated improvement concerns reduced detectability, rather than a guarantee that poisoned graphs cannot be detected.
neurips-2025-stealthy-yet-effective-dist.tldr: DPSBA learns clean-label graph backdoors that reduce structural and semantic anomalies while retaining high reported attack success.

paragraphs: System-1.5 Reasoning targets the computational cost of producing lengthy intermediate reasoning. Reasoning in hidden states can reduce language output, but the authors argue that treating every reasoning step equally still wastes computation. Their framework adapts effort to the importance of different tokens and steps, combining latent-space reasoning with two kinds of shortcuts.

A depth shortcut lets non-critical tokens exit early through lightweight adapter branches, while critical tokens continue through deeper Transformer layers. A step shortcut reuses hidden states across decoding steps to bypass trivial steps. Training uses two stages of self-distillation: natural-language reasoning is first transferred into continuous latent thought, and full-path latent reasoning is then transferred into the adaptive shortcut paths.

On GSM8K, the method reports reasoning performance comparable to traditional chain-of-thought fine-tuning while accelerating inference by more than 20 times and reducing generated tokens by 91.0% on average. These findings support selective computation in the evaluated setting. The approach addresses both the depth used for individual tokens and the number of intermediate decoding steps, rather than relying solely on shorter verbal explanations.
neurips-2025-system-1-5-reasoning-traver.tldr: System-1.5 Reasoning learns adaptive shortcuts through model depth and latent reasoning steps, reporting large inference savings with comparable GSM8K performance.

paragraphs: Generalized games allow the strategies available to one player to depend on the strategies chosen by others. This dependence makes them relevant to economic settings with interlocking choices and constraints. The paper investigates the computational difficulty of finding correlated equilibria in these games, where familiar tractability expectations from other multiplayer settings may no longer apply.

A crucial distinction is between finding an equilibrium with a desirable social outcome and finding any equilibrium at all. Earlier work established that maximizing social welfare over correlated equilibria in generalized games is NP-hard. That result still left open whether an efficient algorithm could find an equilibrium without requiring it to optimize welfare. The paper directly addresses this remaining question.

The authors prove that finding an equilibrium is PPAD-complete. This supplies a computational hardness classification for the basic search problem, even without the additional welfare objective. It answers the open tractability question negatively in the complexity-theoretic sense used by the paper. The contribution is therefore a boundary on general equilibrium computation, rather than an algorithm for selecting a particularly favorable equilibrium.
neurips-2025-the-complexity-of-correlate.tldr: Finding any correlated equilibrium in generalized games is PPAD-complete, extending the difficulty beyond welfare-maximizing equilibrium selection.

paragraphs: WALL-E addresses the mismatch between a language model's prior knowledge and the actual rules of a particular environment. That mismatch can make the model an unreliable predictor for planning. The proposed world alignment process adds symbolic knowledge learned from exploration, allowing environment-specific information to complement what the language model already knows without model training.

Language models extract action rules, knowledge graphs, and scene graphs from exploration trajectories and encode them as executable code. WALL-E then combines this aligned world model with model-predictive control. A language-model agent plans future actions by interacting with the model, supplying an efficient look-ahead optimizer. The system uses this combination of language-model planning and symbolic regulation without reinforcement learning.

On Mars, the authors report success-rate gains of 16.1%–51.6% over baselines and score gains of at least 61.7%. On ALFWorld, WALL-E reaches 98% success after four iterations. The findings support environment-specific world alignment as a way to improve planning and learning efficiency in these evaluated environments, connecting extracted rules to the predictions used to choose future actions.
neurips-2025-wall-e-world-alignment-by-n.tldr: WALL-E extracts executable environment knowledge from exploration and combines it with language-model planning to improve agent performance without reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can provide learned priors for reconstructing images, but conventional score-based training may struggle when Gaussian noise has different strengths or correlations across directions. The difficulty arises from covariance-matrix inversion in the denoising training objective. This paper introduces Whitened Score diffusion to accommodate such structured noise without that inversion.

The framework uses stochastic differential equations and learns a whitened score function instead of the standard score. This enables stable training with arbitrary Gaussian forward noising processes. The authors also establish an equivalence with flow matching for arbitrary Gaussian noise and allow tailored spectral inductive biases. These properties make the noise structure a configurable part of the prior used for imaging reconstruction.

Experiments cover computational imaging tasks using CIFAR, CelebA at 64 by 64 pixels, and CelebA-HQ at 256 by 256 pixels. Priors trained with anisotropic Gaussian noising consistently outperform conventional isotropic-noise diffusion priors in these evaluations. The results support matching the diffusion framework to structured noise, while the mathematical reformulation removes a training obstacle to doing so.
neurips-2025-whitened-score-diffusion-a-.tldr: Whitened Score diffusion avoids covariance inversion and learns structured-noise image priors that outperform isotropic diffusion priors in the reported experiments.
